Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the Q2 FY '26-'27 Earnings Conference Call 
of The Karur Vysya Bank. We have with us today the management team of KVB represented 
by Mr. Ramesh Babu, MD and CEO; Mr. Chandrasekaran, Chief Operating Officer; Chief 
General Manager, Mr. Ramshankar; and Mr. Ramasamy, CFO. 
 
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an 
opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need 
assistance during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on 
your touchtone phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. B. Ramesh Babu, MD and CEO, to take us through the 
highlights of the quarter gone by, after which we will open the floor for questions. Over to 
you, sir. 
B. Ramesh Babu: 
Yes. Thank you, Sagar. Thank you. Good evening to all of you. On behalf of The Karur Vysya 
Bank, I extend a warm welcome to everyone joining our bank's Q2 Earnings Call for the 
financial year '26-'27. Our financial results and accompanying presentation have been made 
available on our website, and we trust you have had the opportunity to review them thoroughly 
in advance of this meeting. 
 
The domestic economy showed resilience in the first half of the current financial year. Despite 
continued global uncertainty and the conflict, the supply side pressures were alleviated by 
proactive policy measures by the government that ensured adequate supply of key inputs. 
System liquidity surplus surged in September 2026, mainly on account of Reserve Bank of 
India's swap facilities. Bank credit growth became broad-based and strengthened further. 
 
As discussed in our previous 2 earnings calls during the current year, we had indicated that 
financial year '26, '27 would be characterized by cautious and moderated growth. We had also 
emphasized the importance of navigating the evolving operating environment with discipline 
ensuring that business growth is pursued without compromising on the portfolio quality. 
 
We are pleased to report that our key performance indicators are broadly in line with the 
guidance shared earlier. The business growth has been balanced and broad-based with 
sustained performance across our 3 key priorities: growth, profitability and asset quality. This 
reflects the continued strength and resilience of our operating performance since the year's 
outset. 
 
As of 30th September 2026, the bank's total business reached INR2,39,712 crores, reflecting 
our sustained growth momentum in the second quarter with an overall business increase of 5% 
quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year growth of 18%. Advances rose to INR1,11,589 crores 
representing a growth of 7% quarter-on-quarter, while deposits increased to INR1,28,123 
crores, achieving quarter-on-quarter growth rate of 5%. 
 
The composition of our advances portfolio remained broadly stable during the quarter with 
RAM segment continuing to account for 86% of the portfolio and the corporate segment 
contributed to the remaining 14%.

The Commercial business segment continued to demonstrate an 8% growth over the previous 
quarter, driven by higher disbursements in both small business group and business banking 
group. So it comes to around 24% quarter-on-quarter, we can say the disbursement growth. 
The growth came predominantly in sectors like engineering, wholesale trade, commercial real 
estate, metal products, retail trade, textiles and transport operators. 
 
Tailor-made products such as GST surrogate for customers with limited financial data and 
open term loan product started during the March quarter have crossed INR450 crores 
outstanding at the end of this quarter. Small business group relationship manager model is 
gaining momentum, and this team has added 228 - new-to-bank customers during the quarter. 
 
Retail advances increased by 5% quarter-on-quarter, primarily driven by growth in mortgage 
loans and personal loans, sequentially down by 1% over the previous quarter. Mortgage loans 
registered a growth of 12% over the previous quarter. Personal loans grew by 11% over the 
previous quarter, driven by secured PL and unsecured business loans equally. 
 
Retail jewel loans marginally declined by 1% during the quarter. We did not reduce the pricing 
in retail jewel loan segment to have a calibrated growth and hence, declined sequentially. The 
agriculture loan portfolio recorded a growth of 4% during the quarter. The increase in oil 
prices due to Gulf market prices, coupled with a moderation in agriculture commodity prices 
provided support for the business growth to some extent. 
 
Favorable expectation of the monsoon in the third quarter, coupled with favorable growth 
indicators of the growth in Agri inputs, the overall outlook remains neutral. Agri-jewel loans 
constituted 92% of the portfolio and other Agri loans constituted 8%. 
 
The overall LTV is maintained at 67% for Agriculture Gold loans and 59% for non-Agri Gold 
loans as on 30th September 2026. We closely monitor the LTV levels, any breach triggers an 
automated alert to the branches. The overall jewel loan portfolio of the bank stood at 
INR32,153 crores, constituting 29% of the total advances. 
 
Our endeavor is to keep the same between 35% of the total advances or 32% in terms of the 
total exposure levels. Suppose if you look at 32% of the total exposure level, even then we will 
be 26%, 27%. If we look at the outstanding, it will be around 29%. So that way, in both the 
cases, we have sufficient room available for us for the growth in the jewel loan portfolio. 
 
The corporate and institutional loan portfolio has grown by 12% during the quarter. The credit 
demand was seen in the segment like EPC, infrastructure sectors, commercial real estate, 
capital market participants and selective capex in textiles and NBFCs. Even though the 
corporate portfolio has been growing well in the last 2 quarters, the average ticket size of the 
portfolio still remained at INR42 crores at the end of Q2. 
 
We continued our focus on credit substitutes and had a growth of around INR500 crores during 
the quarter. Our focus would be on ETB customers with an external rating of A and above on 
this segment.

Our YTD growth is 13% in advances. As a word of caution, YTD growth should not be 
construed and considered as an indicator for the full year growth. We had indicated in the 
beginning of the year that we would grow by 1% to 2% above the industry growth. 
 
With the spurt in credit growth scenario in the industry, we would tread cautiously and look for 
calibrated growth of 18% to 20% for this financial year. The bank's liability business 
constitutes 53% of the total business book of the bank. Our deposits grew by 5% during the 
quarter, driven by gains in both retail term deposits and CASA. 
 
A key highlight of the quarter was the strong momentum in CASA. Current account balance 
increased by INR592 crores, representing a 5% growth during the quarter, while savings 
account balances grew by INR897 crores, again, reflecting a 4% increase over the previous 
quarter. Consequently, CASA balance increased by INR1,489 crores during Q2, supported by 
strong traction in operating accounts, transaction banking relationships. 
 
Our CASA growth continues to be relationship-led. Existing customers contributed nearly to 
60% of the incremental CASA growth, while new customer acquisition accounted for the 
balance. That reflects  both deeper engagement with our customer base and sustained 
acquisition momentum. 
 
Retail deposits remained a key growth engine during the quarter. Retail term deposits 
witnessed healthy traction, supported by calibrated pricing actions undertaken to fund 
advances growth while maintaining a disciplined approach towards wholesale funding.  
 
The bank continued to preserve the granularity and resilience of its deposit franchise with 
retail TD contributing nearly 73% of the total deposits, term deposits and with RTD growing at 
6% quarter-on-quarter with the quarterly growth of INR3,902 crores. The RBI's relaxation on 
FCNRB interest rate ceilings has enabled the bank to source incremental FCNRB deposits of 
around INR680 crores during this quarter, indicating smaller uptick in the NRI business. 
 
Regarding margins, we had provided a guidance in the range of 3.7 to 3.8 for the financial year 
2026-27, about the NIM. I am pleased to report that we were able to maintain our net interest 
margin at 4.26% for this quarter also. If you look at including the one-off recovery, so interest 
recovery, 8 basis points from the written-off accounts, it comes to 4.34%. It was like more or 
less like previous quarter. 
 
The cost of deposits increased marginally by 4 basis points on a sequential basis as rates of 
deposits were increased during the first quarter. And that way, the repricing of deposits, what 
all happened during Q2 and the fresh acquisition, we had to pay a relatively higher rate 
because we have revised the rates in the first quarter. 
 
Funding costs are likely to remain under upward pressure due to RBI's policy tightening, 
liquidity absorption and competition for deposits. However, immediate pressure may not be on 
the bank due to increase in deposit rates and strong FCNR flows still feeding the credit growth. 
So it may have an effect and likely run like this for next 2 to 3 months with the existing rates.

The yield on advances increased by 8 basis points during this quarter and remained at 10.09%. 
EBLR book increased from 55% to 57% compared to the previous quarter. The fixed rate loan 
book remained at 34% and MCLR-linked book reduced from 9% to 7%. 
 
As the market is flushed with liquidity on account of FCNRB flows, we expect huge 
competition in pricing from few banks, and it may bring down the yield going forward. So 
yield on investments dropped marginally by 4 basis points during the quarter at 6.79% from 
6.83% in the previous quarter.  
 
The marginal dip in portfolio yield during Q2 is partly attributable to the investment mix. 
Mutual fund investment mix and mutual fund investment made during quarter 2, the returns 
are computed to NAV appreciation. They are recognized separately and they do not form part 
of the interest income. In the recent monetary policy meeting, RBI had increased the repo rates 
by 25 basis points. 
 
So in view of what we have said earlier and some sort of visibility what we had and 
considering our pricing methodology of the loan book also, so we may end up above 4% or 4% 
plus NIM for the full year. The operating profit for the quarter was at INR1,162 crores, 
reflecting a 14% increase compared to the same quarter in the previous year and 6% growth 
sequentially. 
 
Net interest income has grown by 25% year-on-year and 5% sequentially. The recalibrated 
asset mix and yield optimization continued to result in net interest income growth. However, 
noninterest income for the period remained flat at INR435 crores sequentially. 
 
So our operating expenses for the quarter stood at INR770 crores, representing a marginal 
increase of INR1 crores sequentially. As discount rates went up by 40 basis points during the 
quarter, AS-15 requirements were lower by INR28 crores compared to previous quarter. This 
compensated the increase in core salary costs, which went up by 8% due to DA increase and 
ESOP related provisions. 
 
Other operating expenses have also remained flat compared to previous quarter. Net profit for 
the quarter was INR788 crores, an increase of 4% quarter-on-quarter and 37% year-on-year. 
During the quarter under review, an allocation of INR94 crores was made towards NPA 
migrations, standard assets, restructured assets and INR25 crores additionally, we have 
provided towards the floating provisions, resulting in a credit cost of 0.43% on an annualized 
basis. 
 
With respect to ECL provisioning guidelines, the bank has maintained adequate provisions and 
buffers through floating and prudential provisions over the past few years. Based on our 
internal assessment, so we feel we will be able to manage with the provisions, what all we 
have made. If at all something is required, we'll be able to take care of that the earnings what 
we have.

The total provisions to advances is at 1.65%, which should take care of the transition. The 
ROA for this quarter stands at 2.1%, marginally lower by 1 basis point from previous quarter. 
We expect ROA for the full year to be more than 2%. 
 
Gross slippages for the quarter amounted to INR123 crores, representing 0.44% annualized, 
0.11% of the loan book sequentially; it is lower from INR138 crores. SMA 30+ levels 
remained at 0.22%, same as of previous quarter. We are confident in our ability to maintain the 
slippage ratio below 1% levels as we have previously indicated through ongoing diligent 
account monitoring. 
 
Owing to reduce slippages, improved recoveries and upgrades as well as write-offs, our gross 
NPAs declined marginally by 5 basis points to 0.69%. Our net NPA reduced by 1 basis point 
to 0.18%, and we are committed to maintaining net NPA at below 1% of our loan portfolio. 
The proportion of our standard restructured loan portfolio has further decreased to 0.33% of 
our total loans and continues to perform satisfactorily. 
 
Notably, a substantial portion is secured by collateral and we also maintained a provision of 
40.1% for the standard restructured loan portfolio. Our CRAR Basel III continues to be healthy 
and is at 17.97%, providing us comfortable headroom for growth. 
 
Our liquidity coverage ratio for the quarter is at 129%, and we would be maintaining this in the 
range of 115% to 120%. We opened 20 branches, including 2 branches in the first quarter 
during the half year ended September 2026. We have planned for opening 50 branches during 
the current financial year, and we would be completing 26 branches before the end of next 
quarter and balance before the year-end. 
 
So that way, major part of the branch expansion load will be taken care of before the 
December end. As reported in the monetary policy statement, going forward, India's 
macroeconomic outlook remains resilient, supported by domestic demand and strengthening 
investment despite persistent global uncertainties. 
 
The outlook remains vulnerable to geopolitical developments, volatility in global energy 
markets and weather-related uncertainties. Weak monsoons, coupled with strong El Niño, 
protracted geopolitical tensions, rising international commodity prices, additional frictions in 
the global trade and tightening of global financial conditions could adversely impact the 
growth outlook. 
 
While we remain mindful of the evolving operating environment, our focus remains steady on 
prudent calibrated growth, granularized and to focus on operational efficiency, customer 
centricity and disciplined risk management. This approach gives us confidence in delivering 
sustainable value to all stakeholders. 
 
I would like to express my sincere gratitude to all the investors, analysts and stakeholders for 
their continued confidence and ongoing support. We are committed to upholding this trust 
through continued strong performance in the future. To sum up, our guidance for credit growth 
would be between 18% to 20% for the financial year '26-'27.
